title: Customer Network Authorization Ledger & Compact Audit-API (PRD - WIP)
content:
Context:
We need a lightweight, customer-facing authorization ledger and compact audit API for private deployments that balances regulatory auditability with operational cost. Current feedback: customers want an append-only canonical trace of network changes and approval events they can push to their SIEMs, and our operators want a compact, query-friendly API that doesn’t explode storage or latency budgets.

Problem statement:
- Private deployments require tamper-evident records for: VPC handshakes, firewall rule changes, operator-initiated rollbacks, delegated customer approvals, and ephemeral credential issuance.
- Existing bulky JSON blobs and per-request full-event replication are expensive for long retention windows and slow for small queries (search by change id / time range).
- Customers want both human-readable proofs for audits and machine-friendly compact logs for ingestion.

Goals (MVP):
1) Provide an append-only ledger where every network-relevant change/authorization generates a canonical, compact record: {event_id, actor, type, timestamp, delta_hash, approval_chain_ref}.
2) Offer a compact audit API that supports range queries, indexed by event_id/time/customer-id and returns compact records plus optional human-friendly expansion on demand.
3) Include immutable, signed checkpoints (daily/hourly) that customers can verify using a public verification key (support KMS/HSM integration).
4) Surface an operator + customer approval flow UI that wires to the ledger events and produces the approval_chain_ref.
5) Keep storage cost predictable: default retention 90 days, tiered cold storage options for 1y+ exports.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Full-blown blockchain or consensus across customer networks (out of scope).
- Replacing customer SIEMs — we provide export hooks, not a full replacement.

User stories:
- As a Platform Security Engineer (customer), I want an immutable record of every VPC handshake so I can demonstrate chain-of-authority during audits.
- As an SRE on Redwood, I want a compact index to quickly find the change that caused a degradation without scanning multi-MB JSON entries.
- As a Product Manager, I want to show customers a simple UI with pending approvals and a one-click proof download for compliance teams.

Key requirements:
Functional:
- FR1: Emit ledger entry for: VPC link create/delete, route table changes, firewall rule create/update/delete, delegated admin grant/revoke, operator-initiated rollbacks, certificate/key rotations related to private deployment networking.
- FR2: Each ledger entry must include a stable event_id (UUIDv7), canonical timestamp (RFC3339), actor (principal id), event_type, small delta_hash (SHA256 of canonical delta), and pointer to optional verbose document stored in object storage.
- FR3: Provide GET /v1/compact-audit?start=...&end=...&actor=... with pagination and an efficient index.
- FR4: Provide GET /v1/compact-audit/{event_id}?expand=true to fetch the verbose document when needed.
- FR5: Periodic signed checkpoints: checkpoint manifests signed by Redwood KMS key; support verification by customer using public key.

Non-functional:
- NFR1: API 95th percentile latency for compact queries < 120ms (cold cache), < 40ms (warm).
- NFR2: Append throughput up to 500 events/s per region for peak onboarding bursts.
- NFR3: Default retention 90 days in hot store, economic cold tier at 1+ years with chunked retrieval.
- NFR4: Storage cost per event < $0.0005 (target).
- NFR5: All ledger writes must be durable (ack after WAL + replicate to 3 nodes in region).

Security & Compliance:
- Signed checkpoints integrate with customer KMS via public key distribution. Support customers bringing their own verification keys (BYOK verify-only).
- Access control: ledger read scopes separated from verbose document access (so that compliance teams can get proofs without exposing incidental secrets).
- Audit retention policies configurable; support SOC2 evidence export (zip of checkpoint + signed manifest + verbose docs for timeframe).
- Encrypt verbose documents at rest with platform-managed keys; option for customer-managed keys for enterprise customers.

Design sketch (high-level):
- Ingest path: event generator (control-plane, operator console, customer-initiated API) -> canonicalizer service (normalizes delta, computes delta_hash) -> ledger-writer (append-only segment store with compact index) -> object-store for verbose docs (S3/compatible) -> checkpointer signs compact segment checkpoints and rotates.
- Data model (compact record): event_id | ts | actor | event_type | delta_hash | verbose_doc_ref | approval_chain_ref | region | customer_id
- Verbose document stored separately: full JSON of change + context links (Jira keys, Slack thread ids, diff). Only fetched on expand.

Approval flow (operator + customer):
- Approval surface: in Console under Private > Network > Pending Approvals. Each approval generates an approval_record in ledger with approval_chain_ref that is itself a compact record (signatures from approvers).
- Delegated approvals: supports scoped tokens that customers can issue to their own operators (expiring, scope-limited) — these tokens are logged as ledger events.

APIs (MVP endpoints):
- POST /v1/ledger/events (internal only) -> 202 accepted with event_id
- GET /v1/compact-audit?start=&end=&event_type=&actor=&page_token= -> returns list[compact_record]
- GET /v1/compact-audit/{event_id}?expand=false -> returns compact_record (expand true fetches verbose doc)
- GET /v1/checkpoints?start=&end= -> signed checkpoint manifests (for customer verification)
- POST /v1/exports -> kicks off SOC2 / ad-hoc evidence bundle export (async)

Operational considerations:
- Indexing: primary index by customer_id+ts and secondary by actor/event_type. Use time-partitioned segments to GC old segments cheaply.
- Compaction: periodically compact contiguous segments and emit a compacted checkpoint to reduce read amplification.
- Backfill & replay: tooling to rehydrate ledger for migrations (idempotent write with event_id dedupe).
- Multi-region replication: replicate checkpoints and compact indices across active regions; verbose docs live in regional buckets with cross-region replication optional.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal prototype, 4w): canonicalizer + segment writer + basic GET by event_id. Connect a couple of test events from control-plane.
- Phase 1 (MVP, 8w): compact API read endpoints, checkpoint signer, Console integration (pending approvals list read-only), export hook. Early alpha with 2 pilot customers.
- Phase 2 (enterprise features, 6w): BYOK verification keys, delegated approval tokens, configurable retention, SOC2 export finish, KMS/HSM glue.

Metrics & success criteria:
- Adoption: 2 pilot customers ingesting proof bundles within 3 months.
- Performance: compact query p95 < 120ms; expand fetch < 300ms median.
- Cost: average storage per event <$0.0005 after compaction.
- Reliability: ledger write durability 99.99% (monthly).

Open questions / risks:
- Q1: Should we support customer-hosted verification endpoints (push model) vs. customers pulling checkpoints? Tradeoffs: push reduces customer work but complicates keys/rotation.
- Q2: How to represent operator ephemeral secrets in verbose docs without leaking? Need redact policy and automated redaction pipeline.
- Risk: If verbose docs become too large (e.g., full diffs with attachments), expand flow will be slow. Need size cap and attach-as-artifact model.

Tasks / next steps (immediate):
- Product: finalize API contract doc + example payloads (owner: Maya). JIRA: PD-8421 ticket assigned.
- Eng: prototype canonicalizer, choose segment store tech (leveldb on SSD vs. write-optimized append store). (owner: Arjun)
- Security: draft redact rules and KMS verify flow (owner: Lucille).
- UX: wireframes for Pending Approvals panel + proof download (owner: Ravi).

Notes / references:
- Related: PD-7902 (operator VPC handover UX) , PD-8120 (private onboarding checklist).
- Slack: #private-deploy-ops thread "ledger-prototype" (links/threads embedded in Confluence).

Appendix (example compact record - illustrative):
- event_id: e7f8c9a2-...
- ts: 2025-02-28T15:03:22Z
- actor: svc:control-plane@redwood-internal
- event_type: vpc_peering_create
- delta_hash: 1f8b3e... (sha256)
- verbose_doc_ref: s3://redwood-priv-docs/2025/02/28/e7f8c9a2.json
- approval_chain_ref: chain:2025-02-28:appr-91

Draft language intentionally terse; will iterate on API shapes and UI mocks.
